headline: Morning clouds and fog, then milder afternoon sun through midweek; a weakening Friday front may bring higher-elevation rain.
summary: A ridge of high pressure (a broad area of sinking, dry air) that brought recent dry, foggy mornings is moving east, and light winds are now bringing cooler, damp ocean air inland. Forecasters expect a familiar pattern to continue at least through midweek: low, flat clouds called stratus, and sometimes fog, over the Puget Sound lowlands in the morning, then afternoon sunshine. Dry weather is expected through Tuesday night. Daytime highs should drop a few degrees from recent days to more typical early-October levels. Monday's clouds may take a bit longer to clear than recently, and Monday could be a little cooler. Forecasters thought the clouds would likely keep fog from becoming widespread, though the aviation section still expects some very low visibility overnight in the interior lowlands, with clearing around 11 AM to 2 PM Monday. Temperatures rise slightly Wednesday and Thursday as a weak ridge builds off the California coast. A cold front is expected Friday, but it should weaken as it crosses the region. Higher elevations have the best chance of rain, and the lowlands have a lower chance. Whether or not it rains, Friday and the weekend turn cooler. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry, mild pattern and that the front will arrive and weaken, but less sure of timing: the GFS model shows Friday evening or night, while the ECMWF model and most ensemble members (many runs of one model with slightly different starting conditions) favor Friday afternoon and evening. The front is still several days away, so other changes are possible. No land watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect. A Small Craft Advisory for strong winds and rough water is in effect for the central and eastern Strait of Juan de Fuca until 5 AM Monday.
